problem: Existing VLN and object-nav systems (end-to-end, VLA, foundation-model modular) assume explicitly named single targets and cannot decompose abstract multi-target instructions (e.g. 'rain' -> umbrella, rain jacket, rain boots). They also over-rely on neural semantic cues, ignore geometric frontiers, and wander aimlessly or run heavy VLMs at every step.
motivation: Real robots must follow abstract, implicit-semantics instructions in large unseen environments within limited time. This needs both logical task decomposition and efficient exploration on edge hardware. The paper separates slow VLM reasoning (asynchronous planner grounded in symbolic memory) from fast lightweight-detector-driven exploration with symbolic heuristics.
key_idea: Combine a VLM task planner grounded in a symbolic 3D scene graph plus best-view image memory with an exploration system that fuses open-vocabulary detector scores and symbolic geometric heuristics (distance, unknown area, instance-verification points).
insight: Splitting the pipeline into an asynchronous VLM planner and a lightweight detector-based explorer avoids per-step VLM latency (SG-Nav times out with MTUR ~1.0) while keeping reasoning quality. Ablations show instance-based target points matter most in cluttered semantic scenes (Apartment sim 87.5->70.8) and curiosity terms matter in large open scenes (Real Outdoor 77.8->55.6).
method: Unified Memory System: Hydra-inspired 3D scene graph with object nodes (centroid, best detection score, viewpoint pose, best-view RGB) and room nodes (morphological room segmentation, LLM-labelled, edges by spatial inclusion).
NeSy Task Planner: Qwen3-VL decomposes abstract instructions into 'exploration' and 'go to' subtasks, keeps a target list, and replans after each subtask using the memory.

Coarse-to-fine target verification: the scene graph filters the top-k (e.g. 3) candidates by detection confidence; the VLM then checks their best-view images and neighbor nodes to pick the one that matches the instruction.
Frontier-based target points: frontier cells detected in the forward FoV wedge, clustered by BFS, represented by centroids or sampled points.
Instance-based target points (IBTP): YOLO-World/FastSAM detections above threshold become goal candidates to approach and verify.

NeSy scoring: VL score from a Gaussian mixture over detections with FoV weighting C(Δθ), plus distance weighting 1/(1+d) and unknown-area weighting 1-exp(-k·ratio); S = w_dist·S_dist + w_VL·S_VL·S_unknown.
Goal selection and planning: pick the highest-S_VL instance point if any, else the highest-S_NeSy frontier; FAR Planner does collision-free path planning.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (frozen planner) + YOLO-World and FastSAM (frozen detectors)
setting.observation: RGB-D cameras (5 on Spot in sim; RealSense D455 on the real robot) + LiDAR (Livox Mid-360) + odometry
setting.action_space: goal points on a 2D occupancy map, executed by the FAR Planner (waypoint/path following)
setting.simulator: HabitatSim (indoor DARPA TIAMAT) and IsaacSim (outdoor) plus real world

numbers.eval_set_note: 8 abstract tasks x 3 trials per environment

numbers_note: SR/SPL/MTUR come from tables; no standard VLN benchmarks (R2R, etc.) were evaluated. SPL is printed as a 0-1 fraction. The abstract reports 83.4% indoor / 75% outdoor SR and 86.3% real-world SR as aggregates.
results: VL-Nav reaches 75.0-87.5% SR on the four DARPA TIAMAT sim scenes, versus 12.5-25.0% for the strongest baseline ApexNav, and lower MTUR. In real-world tests it reaches 77.8-91.7% SR (86.3% overall) with SPL up to 0.812, beating VLFM (SR 44.4-75.0%, SPL up to 0.556).
limitations: Evaluated on a custom DARPA TIAMAT benchmark and small real-world trial counts rather than standard VLN benchmarks, so comparisons are limited (SG-Nav/ApexNav were not run on the real robot).
The planner needs a remote RTX 4090 laptop for Qwen3-VL-8B, and the symbolic memory is static, with no temporal reasoning or moving-target tracking.
Real-world baseline VLFM was modified (YOLO-World/FastSAM instead of BLIP-2), so it is not the original VLFM.
